cl_dc_fts_detects_fentanyl.q: Do fentanyl test strips show fentanyl when it is there?
cl_dc_fts_detects_fentanyl.short: In lab tests, strips found fentanyl in 104 of 106 drug samples that had it.
cl_dc_fts_detects_fentanyl.but: Lab staff did these tests, mostly with one brand. Testing at home was not studied.
how: Two labs tested strips on 106 police-seized drug samples that had fentanyl. The strips showed it in 104.
A lab machine had already found fentanyl in all of these samples. Samples with very little fentanyl were not tested this way.
Strips can find very small amounts of fentanyl. But the smallest amount found differed up to 25 times between studies and batches.
It also depended on how a faint line was read. Trained staff did all of these tests.

freq.what: seized samples with fentanyl showed it on the strip
freq.note: 104 of 106 police-seized samples in which a lab machine had already found fentanyl. One brand, read by trained staff in two labs, 2017.

cl_dc_fts_false_positives.q: Can a fentanyl strip show fentanyl when there is none?
cl_dc_fts_false_positives.short: Sometimes. Large amounts of meth, MDMA or two medicines made strips positive with no fentanyl there.
cl_dc_fts_false_positives.but: These were lab tests, mostly of one drug at a time. How often it happens when people test their own drugs is not known.
how: Of 104 seized samples in which a lab machine found no fentanyl, 6 still read positive on the strip.
In the lab, strong solutions of meth or MDMA turned strips positive. So did two medicines, diphenhydramine and lidocaine. Cocaine and several other drugs did not.
It took thousands of times more of these drugs than the smallest amount of fentanyl the same strips could find.

With take-home strips, 28 in 100 crystal meth samples showed fentanyl, against 5 in 100 other samples tested on site by staff. The authors think most were false positives. No lab checked these results.

freq.what: seized samples in which a lab machine found no fentanyl still read positive
freq.note: 6 of 104 samples, one brand, two labs. Some may have held fentanyl, or a related drug, in amounts too small for the lab machine to find.

cl_dc_fts_analogues.q: Do fentanyl strips pick up drugs related to fentanyl, like carfentanil?
cl_dc_fts_analogues.short: In lab tests, strips found most related drugs, but not all. Carfentanil needed large amounts.
cl_dc_fts_analogues.but: These were mostly pure drugs in water, tested by lab staff. The largest study reported no repeat tests.
how: One lab tested 28 related drugs on four brands. At high amounts, 21 to 24 of them showed up.
At lower amounts, only 5 to 12 of the 23 tested showed up.
Three never showed up on any brand. Carfentanil showed only at high amounts, and never on one brand.
A second lab found 11 of 13 related drugs on all five batches of one brand. On two of the three newer batches, carfentanil showed only in very large amounts.

cl_dc_fts_brands_lots.q: Do all fentanyl strips work the same?
cl_dc_fts_brands_lots.short: No. In lab tests, brands and batches differed. Some batches needed ten times more fentanyl.
cl_dc_fts_brands_lots.but: Each difference comes from one or two lab studies, and why batches differed is not known.
how: Batches of one brand bought in 2021 needed ten times more fentanyl to show it than batches bought in 2017.
With no fentanyl there, the 2021 batches read positive with 10 to 40 times less lidocaine or MDMA than the 2017 batches.
Four brands picked up different numbers of related drugs. The one that found the most at a low amount never showed carfentanil. It also read positive with large amounts of vitamin C alone.

Two weeks of heat did not change one kind of strip. Strips more than four years out of date still worked, but needed more fentanyl than their label said. No new strips of that kind were tested to compare.

cl_dc_nitazene_strips.short: In lab tests, the strips found most nitazenes. They missed most of one group, called desnitazenes.
cl_dc_nitazene_strips.but: Only pure or nearly pure drugs were tested. Mixed street drugs were not.
how: One lab tested 33 nitazenes. The strips showed 24 of them. They missed 6 of the 7 desnitazenes, even in large amounts.
Six nearly pure powders from the drug market all showed up.
A second lab found the strips did not react to 76 other drugs and cutting agents.
No study tested street drugs where a nitazene is a small part of a mix.

cl_dc_xylazine_strips.short: Strips found xylazine in 37 of 38 samples with enough of it, but often missed small amounts.
cl_dc_xylazine_strips.but: One batch of strips was read in a lab. The samples were residues from used equipment, not powders.
how: A lab tested 100 residue samples wiped from used syringes, bags and pill bottles, and checked them with a lab machine.
With enough xylazine, 37 of 38 read positive. With less, only 6 of 28 did. None of 34 without xylazine read positive.
In pure water, every strip read positive only from 2.5 times the amount the strip is made to find.
Lidocaine, a common cutting agent, also made strips positive. At the one amount tested, they did not react to medetomidine. It is a similar drug used on animals.

freq.title: Out of every 100 samples with xylazine, how many read positive?
pairs: samples with at least the amount the strip is made to find
freq.note: 37 of 38 and 6 of 28 residue samples, one batch of strips, read in a lab.

cl_dc_benzo_strips.q: Do benzodiazepine strips find the newer benzodiazepines sold on the street?
cl_dc_benzo_strips.short: Often not. At one drug-checking service, strips missed 9 of 24 samples with newer benzodiazepines.
cl_dc_benzo_strips.but: A lab checked only some samples. Many were picked because of a suspected overdose.
how: At eight health sites, samples were tested with strips, and a lab checked some of them.
Strips showed newer benzodiazepines in 15 of 24 samples, but in only 8 of 16 with etizolam alone.
They also read positive in 20 of 129 samples in which the lab found none.
In a lab, the same maker's strip never reacted to pure etizolam. An earlier report said similar strips could pick it up in larger amounts, so the two disagree.

freq.what: samples with a newer benzodiazepine showed it on the strip
freq.note: 15 of 24 samples at one drug-checking service, 2018 to 2020. With etizolam alone, 8 of 16.

cl_dc_colour_mdma.q: Do colour tests like Marquis show whether a pill has MDMA in it?
cl_dc_colour_mdma.short: In a lab, experts got MDMA right. Two first-time testers made many mistakes.
cl_dc_colour_mdma.but: One small lab study from 2003, with a kit and pills of that time.
how: Three lab experts read all 35 samples with MDMA as positive, and nearly all of the 4 without MDMA as negative.
Seven MDMA samples also had another drug, like caffeine or amphetamine. The colour looked the same.
Two people new to the kit tested 8 known drugs. One missed both MDMA samples. The other called four other drugs MDMA.
A review says MDA and MDEA, drugs close to MDMA, give a similar colour. It adds that, read by eye, the tests do not show how much MDMA a pill holds.

cl_dc_home_vs_service.q: Do results with take-home strips match testing by trained staff?
cl_dc_home_vs_service.short: For opioids, about the same. For meth and cocaine, take-home strips showed fentanyl far more often.
cl_dc_home_vs_service.but: The two groups tested different samples, and no lab checked which results were right.
how: In 2019, people took strips from ten health sites and used them at home a little over half the time. Staff tested other samples at the sites.
Opioids: 90 in 100 take-home results showed fentanyl, and 89 in 100 on site.
Crystal meth: 28 in 100 take-home results, and 5 in 100 on site. The authors think most of the extra take-home positives were false.
People told the study their own results, often from memory.

freq.title: Out of every 100 crystal meth samples, how many showed fentanyl?
pairs: tested by the person with a take-home strip
tested on site by trained staff
freq.note: 73 of 265 and 5 of 97 samples, British Columbia, 2019. Different samples; no lab checked which results were right.

cl_dc_home_what_tests_miss.q: What can a home test not tell you?
cl_dc_home_what_tests_miss.short: A test for one drug did not show other drugs in the mix, or how much.
cl_dc_home_what_tests_miss.but: Only two small studies tested this directly. The rest is how the tests are made.
how: In one lab study, MDMA samples with caffeine or amphetamine mixed in looked the same on a colour test.
At one drug-checking service, 24 of 159 samples checked by a lab had a newer benzodiazepine. None of the people who brought them expected it. Most also had fentanyl.
Fentanyl strips only show if fentanyl is there. They do not show how much.
No study tested whether a negative result makes a drug less risky.
